# Contributing

Thanks for helping improve this collection. Reproduced defects, compatibility
evidence, documentation corrections, and focused skill improvements are
welcome.

This is a curated collection and a consumer-facing release projection. The
source governed with [remek](https://github.com/benblackthorn/remek) is
authoritative, so a proposed skill change may be reproduced and re-verified
there rather than merged byte-for-byte from a pull request. Public repository
documentation and policy changes can be reviewed directly here.

## Choose the right contribution path

- **Bug or routing problem:** open an issue with the affected skill, exact
  commit, agent host, prompt or command, expected behavior, and sanitized
  reproduction.
- **Documentation correction:** open a focused pull request.
- **Skill improvement:** open an issue or pull request describing the behavior
  change and the evidence behind it. Treat the patch as a proposal until it has
  passed the governed release process.
- **New skill:** open an issue before building it. Explain the distinct job,
  intended users, activation and non-activation cases, dependencies, safety
  boundaries, and why an existing skill cannot own it.
- **Security issue:** follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md); never disclose
  sensitive findings in a public issue or pull request.

Do not directly edit `release-manifest.json`. It is generated by the release
workflow.

## Quality bar for skills

A skill contribution should:

- solve one clear, recurring job with meaningful uplift over generic model
  behavior;
- define positive and contrastive routing so agents know when not to use it;
- keep the normal path understandable from `SKILL.md`;
- state platform, runtime, tool, permission, and network requirements;
- preserve user data and fail safely at destructive boundaries;
- avoid credentials, private content, opaque downloads, and unnecessary
  dependencies;
- include focused verification for observable behavior and reproduced defects;
- carry accurate provenance and licensing for every included file.

Prefer a small complete skill over a broad framework, duplicated guidance, or
speculative extensibility.

## Pull requests

Keep each pull request to one problem. Name every affected skill, describe the
user-visible and routing changes, disclose dependency or permission changes,
and state exactly what you ran.

Repository-wide checks are intentionally generic because individual skills own
their deeper verification:

```bash
gh skill publish --dry-run
git diff --check
```

Also run the documented checks for each affected skill. The full governed gates
run again before a skill projection is released.
